2026-09-07T03:27:33.5057675Z ## MCP Servers Mounted as Shell CLI Commands
2026-09-07T03:27:33.5058601Z 
2026-09-07T03:27:33.5059250Z The following servers are available as CLI commands on `PATH`:
2026-09-07T03:27:33.5060182Z 
2026-09-07T03:27:33.5060886Z - `safeoutputs` — run `safeoutputs --help` to see available tools
2026-09-07T03:27:33.5061850Z 
2026-09-07T03:27:33.5066351Z > **IMPORTANT**: For `safeoutputs` and `mcpscripts`, **always use the CLI commands** listed above instead of the equivalent MCP tools. The CLI wrappers are the preferred interface — do **not** call their MCP tools directly even though they may appear in your tool list.
2026-09-07T03:27:33.5070086Z >
2026-09-07T03:27:33.5079152Z > For `safeoutputs`, treat every successful command as a real write-intent declaration. Do **not** use `safeoutputs` for exploratory probing, auth checks, placeholder payloads, repeated "try again" variants, or manual runtime experiments. When you need a safe-output, emit the final intended call once. If you are not ready to perform the real action, use `noop` or `report_incomplete` instead.
2026-09-07T03:27:33.5085677Z >
2026-09-07T03:27:33.5087285Z > For all other servers listed here, they are **only** available as CLI commands and are **not** available as MCP tools.
2026-09-07T03:27:33.5089066Z 
2026-09-07T03:27:33.5089428Z ### How to Use
2026-09-07T03:27:33.5089900Z 
2026-09-07T03:27:33.5091318Z Each server is a standalone executable on your `PATH`. Invoke it from bash like any other shell command:
2026-09-07T03:27:33.5092726Z 
2026-09-07T03:27:33.5093062Z ```bash
2026-09-07T03:27:33.5094099Z # Call a tool — pass arguments as --name value pairs
2026-09-07T03:27:33.5095482Z <server-name> <tool-name> --param1 value1 --param2 value2
2026-09-07T03:27:33.5097172Z ```
2026-09-07T03:27:33.5097601Z 
2026-09-07T03:27:33.5098406Z **Example** — using the `playwright` CLI:
2026-09-07T03:27:33.5099464Z ```bash
2026-09-07T03:27:33.5100522Z playwright --help                                  # list all browser tools
2026-09-07T03:27:33.5103145Z playwright browser_navigate --url https://example.com
2026-09-07T03:27:33.5106640Z playwright browser_snapshot                        # capture page accessibility tree
2026-09-07T03:27:33.5108353Z ```
2026-09-07T03:27:33.5108769Z 
2026-09-07T03:27:33.5110057Z **Example** — using the `safeoutputs` CLI (safe outputs) when you are ready to emit the final real action:
2026-09-07T03:27:33.5111758Z ```bash
2026-09-07T03:27:33.5112870Z safeoutputs add_comment --issue_number 42 --body "Analysis complete"
2026-09-07T03:27:33.5114630Z ```
2026-09-07T03:27:33.5115073Z 
2026-09-07T03:27:33.5115916Z **Example** — using the `mcpscripts` CLI (mcp-scripts):
2026-09-07T03:27:33.5117084Z ```bash
2026-09-07T03:27:33.5118358Z mcpscripts --help                                  # list all script tools
2026-09-07T03:27:33.5120082Z mcpscripts mcpscripts-gh --args "pr list --repo owner/repo --limit 5"
2026-09-07T03:27:33.5121456Z ```
2026-09-07T03:27:33.5121865Z 
2026-09-07T03:27:33.5122385Z ### Passing Multiple or Complex Arguments (Preferred)
2026-09-07T03:27:33.5123212Z 
2026-09-07T03:27:33.5126014Z **Preferred approach for any tool call with multiple or complex arguments**: supply a JSON object on stdin using `.` as the sentinel. The bridge parses stdin as the argument object, preserving all native types (numbers, booleans, arrays) without shell-quoting issues.
2026-09-07T03:27:33.5130666Z 
2026-09-07T03:27:33.5131050Z ```bash
2026-09-07T03:27:33.5131961Z # Full argument payload as JSON via printf pipe
2026-09-07T03:27:33.5134061Z printf '{"issue_number":42,"body":"### Title\n\nBody paragraph one.\n\nBody paragraph two."}' \
2026-09-07T03:27:33.5136227Z   | safeoutputs add_comment .
2026-09-07T03:27:33.5136854Z 
2026-09-07T03:27:33.5137991Z # Works with any tool — just match the parameter names from <server> <tool> --help
2026-09-07T03:27:33.5140845Z printf '{"title":"Fix: something","body":"Details here","labels":["bug","priority-high"]}' \
2026-09-07T03:27:33.5142488Z   | safeoutputs create_issue .
2026-09-07T03:27:33.5143417Z ```
2026-09-07T03:27:33.5143820Z 
2026-09-07T03:27:33.5145289Z **When pipes are blocked by the bash security policy**, write the payload to a file first and use **file redirection** with the `.` sentinel instead:
2026-09-07T03:27:33.5147070Z 
2026-09-07T03:27:33.5147407Z ```bash
2026-09-07T03:27:33.5149403Z # Step 1 — write the JSON payload to a file using the Write tool or a bash heredoc
2026-09-07T03:27:33.5151105Z # Step 2 — redirect the file into the CLI command using '<'
2026-09-07T03:27:33.5152506Z safeoutputs create_pull_request . < /tmp/payload.json
2026-09-07T03:27:33.5153351Z 
2026-09-07T03:27:33.5154131Z # This is equivalent to piping but does not require a separate command before '|'
2026-09-07T03:27:33.5155691Z safeoutputs add_comment . < /tmp/comment.json
2026-09-07T03:27:33.5156773Z ```
2026-09-07T03:27:33.5157172Z 
2026-09-07T03:27:33.5157584Z > **Why prefer JSON payload mode?**
2026-09-07T03:27:33.5159286Z > - Single operation for any number of arguments — no repeated `--key value` flags
2026-09-07T03:27:33.5161711Z > - Native types (integers, booleans, arrays) are preserved exactly as specified
2026-09-07T03:27:33.5163606Z > - No shell quoting or escaping needed for newlines, quotes, or special characters
2026-09-07T03:27:33.5166836Z > - Agents can construct the payload as a structured object before emitting the command
2026-09-07T03:27:33.5169144Z > - File redirection (`< file`) works even when pipes (`|`) are restricted
2026-09-07T03:27:33.5170193Z 
2026-09-07T03:27:33.5170541Z ### Notes
2026-09-07T03:27:33.5170970Z 
2026-09-07T03:27:33.5172184Z - **Prefer JSON payload mode** (`. < file` or `printf '{...}' | server tool .`) for any call with multiple arguments or complex values
2026-09-07T03:27:33.5175481Z - All parameters can also be passed as `--name value` pairs; boolean flags can be set with `--flag` (no value) to mean `true`
2026-09-07T03:27:33.5178806Z - Use `.` as the only argument to parse stdin as a JSON object (all parameters supplied at once)
2026-09-07T03:27:33.5201435Z - Parameter names with hyphens or underscores are interchangeable (e.g. `issue-number` and `issue_number` both work)
2026-09-07T03:27:33.5204895Z - Output is printed to stdout; errors are printed to stderr with a non-zero exit code
2026-09-07T03:27:33.5278510Z - Run the CLI commands inside a `bash` tool call — they are shell executables, not MCP tools
2026-09-07T03:27:33.5280611Z - These CLI commands are read-only and cannot be modified by the agent
2026-09-07T03:27:33.5281986Z </mcp-clis>
2026-09-07T03:27:33.5282920Z <github-context>
2026-09-07T03:27:33.5284130Z The following GitHub context information is available for this workflow:

2026-09-07T03:27:33.5315817Z relevant top Hacker News stories on technology that can be used today
2026-09-07T03:27:33.5317543Z by large companies. Every weekday, fetch the top 30 stories from the
2026-09-07T03:27:33.5319524Z Hacker News API (https://hacker-news.firebaseio.com/v0/topstories.json),

2026-09-07T03:27:33.5322795Z engineering, cloud infrastructure, AI/ML, developer tooling, or

2026-09-07T03:27:33.5327931Z why it is relevant to enterprise developers. Create a GitHub issue
